In CEUS il tempo dall'iniezione è parte: In CEUS the time from injection is part of the finding. The arterial phase runs from about 10-20 to 30-45 seconds, the portal phase up to 2 minutes, the late phase up to 4-6 minutes. Hepatocellular carcinoma typically shows late (after 60 s) and mild washout; intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and metastases show early (before 60 s) and marked washout ("black" lesion within 2 minutes), often with rim arterial hyperenhancement. For this reason CEUS LI-RADS v2017 has the LR-M category: rim hyperenhancement, or early washout, or marked washout. An LR-M lesion should be biopsied. Pitfall: a nodule that enhances in the arterial phase and then washes out "looks like" hepatocellular carcinoma, but if the washout occurs before 60 seconds or becomes marked within 2 minutes the category is LR-M. In this case the hyperenhancement at 21 s is not clearly rim-like on the still images: the LR-M category arises from the timing and intensity of the washout. On CT/MRI cholangiocarcinoma often shows peripheral enhancement and late centripetal filling (fibrous stroma). CEUS LI-RADS applies to patients at risk of hepatocellular carcinoma: here the clinical history is not provided, but the management (biopsy) does not change.
